quests.instruction: What is a good plan for fruit juice?
quests.correctAnswer: Eat whole fruit most days and have juice only sometimes
options: Eat whole fruit most days and have juice only sometimes
Drink juice every day instead of eating whole fruit
Drink a big glass of juice with every meal and snack
quests.hint: Think about fiber.
quests.explanation: Whole fruit has more fiber and fills you up more, so juice is best as a small extra.
quests.funFact: A small glass is plenty when juice is a treat.

quests.instruction: Many food guides suggest filling about how much of your plate with fruits and vegetables?
quests.correctAnswer: About half
options: About half
Almost none
Only one tiny piece
quests.hint: Think about a colorful plate.
quests.explanation: Many food guides suggest filling about half of your plate with fruits and vegetables.
quests.funFact: A colorful plate usually means a nice variety of foods.

quests.instruction: What does the serving size on a food label tell you?
quests.correctAnswer: How much food the numbers on the label are for
options: How many farms helped to grow and make the food
How much food the numbers on the label are for
How big the whole box or package is in total
quests.hint: Think about what the numbers describe.
quests.explanation: The serving size tells you how much food the numbers on the label are for, and a package can hold more than one serving.
quests.funFact: A small bag of dried fruit can hold more than one serving.

quests.instruction: Why do our bodies need vitamins from foods like fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: They help our bodies work and grow
options: They make us grow taller instantly
They help our bodies work and grow
They replace the need for sleep
quests.hint: Think about what keeps a body healthy.
quests.explanation: Vitamins help our bodies work and grow, and different foods give us different vitamins.
quests.funFact: There are several different vitamins, and different fruits are good sources of different ones.

quests.instruction: You do not like a new fruit the first time. What can help?
quests.correctAnswer: Try a small bite again another day
options: Try a small bite again another day
Never try it again
Eat it only when no one is looking
quests.hint: Tastes can change.
quests.explanation: Tastes can change, and many people need to try a new food several times before they like it.
quests.funFact: Fruit can taste very different when it is ripe, cold or cut a different way.

quests.instruction: Which makes a colorful dessert with no added sugar?
quests.correctAnswer: A fruit salad of berries, melon and kiwi
options: A bowl of sugar with a little cinnamon
A fruit salad of berries, melon and kiwi
A plain bread roll with sweet butter
quests.hint: Think about using fruit's own sweetness.
quests.explanation: A fruit salad uses the natural sweetness of the fruit and adds lots of color.
quests.funFact: Mixing colors makes a fruit salad look and taste more interesting.

quests.instruction: A shop smoothie is made with fruit, syrup and sweetened juice. What is smart to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Read the label or ask what is added
options: Assume it is made only of fresh fruit
Drink three of them to compare them
Read the label or ask what is added
quests.hint: Think about what else might be in the cup.
quests.explanation: Some shop smoothies have added syrup or sweet juice, so reading the label or asking is a smart habit.
quests.funFact: A homemade smoothie lets you choose exactly what goes in.

quests.instruction: Which is a good goal?
quests.correctAnswer: Eat some fruit and vegetables every day
options: Eat fruit only on birthdays and holidays
Skip vegetables and eat only fruit
Eat some fruit and vegetables every day
quests.hint: Think about daily habits.
quests.explanation: Eating some fruit and vegetables every day helps you get many different nutrients.
quests.funFact: Many countries have food guides that encourage fruit and vegetables every day.

quests.instruction: Which is a cold treat you can make from fruit alone?
quests.correctAnswer: Frozen banana pieces blended until creamy
options: Frozen banana pieces blended until creamy
A bowl of syrup mixed with crushed ice
Melted candy poured over crushed ice
quests.hint: Think of a creamy, ice-cream-like texture.
quests.explanation: Blending frozen banana makes a creamy, ice-cream-like treat with no added sugar.
quests.funFact: Some people blend in frozen berries or mango for different flavors.

quests.instruction: Where in a supermarket would you find fresh fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: In the produce section
options: In the cleaning aisle
In the pet food aisle
In the produce section
quests.hint: Think about where fresh fruit and vegetables are displayed.
quests.explanation: The produce section is where fresh fruit and vegetables are displayed.
quests.funFact: The word produce means fresh fruits and vegetables grown on farms.

quests.instruction: A sign next to the apples says "per kilogram." What does it tell you?
quests.correctAnswer: The price for each kilogram
options: How many apples are in a box
How far the apples travelled
The price for each kilogram
quests.hint: Think about weighing fruit at a shop.
quests.explanation: "Per kilogram" tells you the price for each kilogram, so the total depends on the weight you buy.
quests.funFact: Many shops weigh fruit at the checkout or on a scale in the produce section.

quests.instruction: How should you pack groceries so soft fruit does not get squashed?
quests.correctAnswer: Put heavy items at the bottom and soft fruit on top
options: Put the soft fruit at the very bottom of the bag
Put heavy items at the bottom and soft fruit on top
Toss everything in at random, heavy or soft
quests.hint: Think about what should not be squashed.
quests.explanation: Heavy items go at the bottom so they do not crush soft fruit.
quests.funFact: Sturdy fruits like apples and oranges handle a little more pressure than berries.

quests.instruction: Before buying a box of berries, what is smart to check?
quests.correctAnswer: Look through the box for mold or crushed berries
options: Look through the box for mold or crushed berries
Shake the box hard to hear how ripe they are
Smell only the plastic lid and the label
quests.hint: Think about what could be hiding in the box.
quests.explanation: Checking the container for mold or crushed, leaking berries helps you avoid fruit that will spoil quickly.
quests.funFact: Berry containers often have holes to let air through.

quests.instruction: Why is in-season fruit often a good buy?
quests.correctAnswer: There is plenty of it, so it is often fresher and cheaper
options: There is plenty of it, so it is often fresher and cheaper
It is always the biggest and sweetest fruit of the year
It never needs washing before you eat it, ever
quests.hint: Think about what happens when a lot of fruit is ready at once.
quests.explanation: When a fruit is in season, lots of it is ready nearby, so it tends to be fresher, tastier and cheaper.
quests.funFact: Seasons for the same fruit can be different in different countries.

quests.instruction: A 1 kilogram bag of grapes costs 4 coins. A 500 gram bag costs 3 coins. Which is the better value?
quests.correctAnswer: The 1 kg bag
options: The 500 g bag
They cost the same per kilogram
The 1 kg bag
quests.hint: Compare the price for the same amount.
quests.explanation: The 1 kg bag costs 4 coins per kilogram, while the 500 g bag costs 6 coins per kilogram.
quests.funFact: Comparing the price per kilogram helps you compare different sizes fairly.

quests.instruction: Which fruit travels best in a school bag without being squashed?
quests.correctAnswer: Apple
options: Raspberries
Apple
Sliced melon
quests.hint: Think about a firm, whole fruit.
quests.explanation: A firm whole apple handles bumps well, while raspberries and cut melon are delicate.
quests.funFact: Fruits with thick skins, like oranges and bananas, travel well too.

quests.instruction: What helps protect strawberries from being squished in a lunchbox?
quests.correctAnswer: A small hard container with a lid
options: A thin plastic bag at the bottom of the bag
A small hard container with a lid
Loose in a pocket
quests.hint: Think about a little shield.
quests.explanation: A small hard container keeps strawberries from being pressed or squashed.
quests.funFact: A hard container protects delicate fruit from being crushed by other items.

quests.instruction: Which is helpful to pack with juicy fruit like oranges or mangoes?
quests.correctAnswer: A napkin or wet wipe
options: A heavy book
A flashlight
A napkin or wet wipe
quests.hint: Think about sticky fingers.
quests.explanation: Juicy fruit can make fingers sticky, so a napkin or wet wipe is handy.
quests.funFact: Washing hands before and after sticky snacks keeps things tidy.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is mashed to make guacamole?
quests.correctAnswer: Avocado
options: Avocado
Mango
Melon
quests.hint: Think of a creamy green fruit.
quests.explanation: Guacamole is made by mashing ripe avocado with lime, salt and other ingredients.
quests.funFact: The name guacamole comes from an old Aztec word for avocado sauce.

quests.instruction: Which fruit pieces stay on a skewer best for fruit kebabs?
quests.correctAnswer: Firm chunks like melon or pineapple
options: Firm chunks like melon or pineapple
Soft ripe bananas cut into slices
Whole raspberries from a punnet
quests.hint: Think about what holds its shape.
quests.explanation: Firm pieces hold their shape on a stick, while very soft fruit slides off.
quests.funFact: Use blunt sticks for fruit kebabs and ask a grown-up to help.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is best added last to a fruit salad so it stays firm?
quests.correctAnswer: Banana
options: Grapes
Pineapple chunks
Banana
quests.hint: Think about which one turns soft and dark quickly.
quests.explanation: Banana is soft and turns mushy and dark quickly, so it is added just before serving.
quests.funFact: Adding banana last keeps the whole salad looking fresh.

quests.instruction: Which fruit snack is light to carry and does not squash on a long hike?
quests.correctAnswer: Dried apricots
options: Ripe peaches
Dried apricots
Raspberries
quests.hint: Think about a snack that is dry and sturdy.
quests.explanation: Dried apricots are light, chewy and do not squash easily, so they are good for hikes.
quests.funFact: Hikers sometimes mix dried fruit with seeds or nuts into trail mix.

quests.instruction: You are baking bread and want a fruit that mashes easily and adds sweetness. Which is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Very ripe banana
options: Hard green banana
Very ripe banana
A lemon
quests.hint: Think about a soft, sweet fruit.
quests.explanation: Very ripe bananas are soft and sweet, so they mash easily into bread.
quests.funFact: Banana bread is a popular way to use bananas that are past their best.

quests.instruction: A recipe asks for a little lime zest. Which tool is best for the thin green peel?
quests.correctAnswer: A fine grater
options: A fine grater
A rolling pin
A whisk
quests.hint: Think about a tool with tiny sharp holes.
quests.explanation: A fine grater scrapes off just the thin, colorful outer peel.
quests.funFact: A zester is a tool made just for scraping citrus peel.

quests.instruction: Your strawberries are getting soft but are not moldy. What could you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Freeze slices or blend them into a smoothie
options: Leave them on a sunny counter for a week
Freeze slices or blend them into a smoothie
Seal them in a warm bag until they dry out
quests.hint: Think about using them before they spoil.
quests.explanation: Soft strawberries that are not moldy can be sliced and frozen or blended into smoothies or sauces.
quests.funFact: Freezing fruit pieces on a tray first stops them from sticking together.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is the messiest to eat on a long trip?
quests.correctAnswer: Watermelon
options: Apple
Grapes
Watermelon
quests.hint: Think about which one drips.
quests.explanation: Watermelon is very juicy and drips easily, while apples and grapes are tidier.
quests.funFact: Many people eat watermelon outdoors because it is so juicy.

quests.instruction: You are packing fruit for a hot day outdoors. What helps keep it fresh?
quests.correctAnswer: An insulated bag with an ice pack
options: A closed car parked in the sun
An insulated bag with an ice pack
A plastic bag left on a sunny seat
quests.hint: Think about keeping things cool.
quests.explanation: An insulated bag with an ice pack keeps fruit cool and fresh in hot weather.
quests.funFact: Cold packs help keep many foods fresh in hot weather.

quests.instruction: A box has 12 oranges. Four friends share them equally. How many oranges does each friend get?
quests.hint: Share 12 into 4 equal groups.
quests.explanation: 12 divided by 4 is 3, so each friend gets 3 oranges.
quests.funFact: Oranges can be shared as whole fruits or as segments.

quests.instruction: A basket has 8 apples, and half of them are red. How many are red?
quests.hint: Half means two equal parts.
quests.explanation: Half of 8 is 4, so there are 4 red apples.
quests.funFact: Mixed baskets of red and green apples look cheerful.

quests.instruction: Mangoes cost 4 coins each and you have 10 coins. How many mangoes can you buy?
quests.hint: Count how many times 4 fits into 10.
quests.explanation: Two mangoes cost 8 coins. A third would cost 12, which is more than 10.
quests.funFact: Checking prices helps you plan what to buy.
